10.1002_advs.202506749: Organic electrode materials have garnered great attention in recent years, owing to their resource sustainability, structural diversity, and superior compatibility with various ionic species. Among them, quinone-based compounds have attracted particular interest. Notably, compared with para-quinone analogs (e.g., anthraquinone), ortho-quinone-based electrode materials (e.g., phenanthraquinone) demonstrate higher redox potential, which contributes to achieving higher energy density in battery applications. However, their practical applications have been limited by severe solubility in electrolytes, resulting in poor cycle performance. To improve it, two novel phenanthraquinone-derived molecules, 1,4-bis(9,10-phenanthraquinonyl)benzene (BPQB) and 1,3,5-tri(9,10-phenanthraquinonyl)benzene (TPQB), are rationally designed, synthesized, and applied as cathode materials for both lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Comprehensive electrochemical evaluations reveal remarkable cycling stability and rate performance of TPQB. The TPQB cathodes for LIBs achieve a high-capacity retention of 76.8% after 1,000 cycles at 5 C, while exhibiting extraordinary ultra-long cycle life in AZIBs with 93.2% capacity retention over 6,000 cycles at 5 C. Their charge storage mechanisms are elucidated through various characterization methods. The work presents a novel molecular engineering strategy that effectively inhibits the dissolution of phenanthraquinone-derived electrode materials and thus realizes excellent electrochemical performance across diverse battery systems.
10.1002_aenm.202505888: Hydrocarbon (HC) membranes have the potential to significantly enhance the efficiency of water electrolyzers. However, their low mechanical integrity under electrolysis conditions, due to severe swelling, poses a challenge for industrial‐scale applications. Here, we present a 12 µm‐thick sulfonated poly(phenylene sulfone) (sPPS) membrane reinforced with a porous polyethylene (PE) substrate. The PE substrate reduces in‐plane swelling by a factor of 7 (10% vs 69%) and improves mechanical stability (440 MPa vs 50 MPa) in water at 60°C. Under electrolysis conditions, a 24 µm thick sandwich of two reinforced membranes shows stable operation over more than 2000 h in a constant current hold at 1 A cm −2 conducted at 60°C (first 1000 h) and 80°C (remaining 1000 h) with only 6 µV h −1 of voltage deviation within the last 500 h. With a potential of 1.67 V and a hydrogen in oxygen content of 1 vol% at 3 A cm −2 , the PFAS‐free membrane clearly outperforms a state‐of‐the‐art reference (Nafion‐N211: 1.73 V and 1.5 vol% at 3 A cm −2 ).
10.1016_j.apsusc.2025.162977: • Synthesis of pyrrolic Fe–N–C structures derived from hemoglobin. • Synthesis of hollow structures with micropores for rapid mass transport. • Exhibits excellent ORR performance and electrochemical endurance. • The ORR pathway is proposed to elucidate an enhanced ORR activity. Metal-decorated nitrogen-doped carbon (M−N−C) materials have garnered significant attention as potential alternatives to address the high cost of noble metal-based catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction. However, they still face challenges, such as complex synthesis processes, insufficient durability, heterogeneous active sites, and an incomplete understanding of the underlying mechanisms. In this study, a facile method is presented for introducing pyrrole-type Fe–N–C active sites into N-doped carbon (NC) using hemoglobin (Hb) as a precursor. This approach was combined with an engineered hollow morphology to facilitate electrolyte permeation and increase the active surface area. The resulting Fe-embedded hollow N-doped carbon (Fe/hNC) demonstrated improved ORR activity compared to that of NC, featuring an onset potential of 0.916 V vs. RHE and a half-wave potential of 0.833 V vs. RHE in alkaline media, comparable to that of commercial Pt/C. Moreover, the ORR current density was retained at 80 %–90 % of its initial value after the durability test, representing a substantial improvement over the 50 %–60 % retention observed for Pt/C. This design strategy, which combines hollow morphology and specific Fe precursor modification, offers promising avenues for developing efficient catalysts for energy-conversion systems.
10.1016_j.isci.2025.114076: Microplastics are contaminating the environment but also our food and drinking products. In a crucial study, microplastics have been detected in circulating human blood, urging the investigation of the effects of microplastics on human health. Here we aimed to determine the distribution of microplastics after oral exposure in mice and their interactions with and effects on mouse and human innate immune cells. We established that both 1 and 10μm polystyrene (PS) particles penetrated the intestinal epithelium after oral administration and could be detected in blood and liver of mice after ten days of oral administration. Using intravital microscopy we captured the in vivo phagocytosis of 1μm PS by mouse neutrophils in the liver. Pristine PS were barely phagocytosed by primary human phagocytes, however, 1 and 10µm PS pre-incubated with plasma were readily phagocytosed by human neutrophils and monocytes. Plasma-coated 1 and 10μm PS both increased human neutrophil and monocyte cell death but only after phagocytosis. Importantly, neutrophil cell death occurred a few hours after phagocytosing a single coated 10µm PS while PS of 1µm needed to be administered at a ratio of 27 particles per cell to induce significant neutrophil cell death. Neutrophil cell death upon microplastic exposure was characterized by extracellular DNA, which together with other released DAMPs can potentially trigger inflammation. Our findings suggest that microplastics could negatively impact the immune system and human health.
10.1021_acs.estlett.6c00568: Industrial recycling of spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is expanding rapidly, yet its emissions of electrolyte-derived organic contaminants remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we provide the first field evidence that industrial LIB recycling is a significant source of diverse cyclic, linear, and fluorinated carbonates to the indoor environment. Using compound-specific GC-MS/MS, we screened 20 carbonates in 64 dust samples from a representative industrial-scale LIB recycling plant in China. Twelve carbonates were ubiquitously detected, including five cyclic carbonates, six linear carbonates, and one fluorinated carbonate, with total concentrations reaching up to 16,700 ng/g (mean: 3,870 ng/g). The contamination profile was dominated by cyclic carbonates (e.g., propylene carbonate and ethylene carbonate) and volatile linear carbonates, broadly reflecting commercial LIB electrolyte formulations. Notably, the frequent detection of 3,3,3-trifluoropropylene carbonate (TFPC) highlights the emission footprint of advanced fluorinated additives. Strong positive intercompound correlations indicate their corelease from residual electrolytes during LIB pretreatment. These findings significantly expand the chemical footprint of LIB recycling, identifying carbonate electrolytes as another abundant and critical class of new pollutants of emerging concern that necessitate urgent multimedia environmental monitoring and occupational exposure assessments.
10.1021_acsami.5c05429: High Resolution Image Download MS PowerPoint Slide Crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) remains a major challenge for brain-targeted drug delivery. Mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) with tunable size and surface properties are promising vehicles for crossing the BBB. In this study, we explored the potential applications of the chick chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model in combination with nanotherapeutics. We synthesized ∼25 nm MSNs and RITC-conjugated MSNs (RMSNs) with short PEG chains and varying amounts of positively charged molecules, specifically tertiary amine (polyethylenimine, PEI) or quaternary amine (trimethylammonium, TA), to investigate the positive charge effects on BBB penetration. Strongly positively charged TA-modified RMSNs (s-RMSN@PEG/TA, where s denotes strongly positively charged) effectively crossed the chick embryo BBB, whereas PEI-modified RMSNs did not. Although the weakly positively charged formulation (w-MSN@PEG/TA, where w denotes weakly positively charged) exhibited higher Dox loading capacity and a faster release rate, s-MSN@PEG/TA demonstrated superior BBB penetration and drug permeability. Consistent with chick CAM results, RMSN@PEG/TA also penetrated the BBB in mice. Long-chain PEG-modified RMSN@PEG/TA (RMSN@PEG (L) /TA, where L denotes long-chain PEG) showed reduced BBB penetration due to steric hindrance, possibly shielding TA molecules. This study highlights the effectiveness of optimizing short PEG chain density and TA modification for MSN-based BBB crossing without additional biological ligands. Furthermore, the chick CAM model proves to be a valuable alternative to mouse models for assessing BBB crossing of nanoparticles, offering significant research opportunities.
10.1021_acscatal.6c03510: Developing cost-effective and durable oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts is pivotal for advancing proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers toward large-scale hydrogen production. Cobalt manganese spinel oxides (i.e., Co2MnO4) have emerged as promising nonprecious alternatives owing to their tunable composition and intrinsic OER activity. However, their deployment in acidic media is severely constrained by Mn dissolution and sluggish reaction kinetics governed by adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM). Herein, we demonstrate that introducing Ir into Co2MnO4 spinels serves a dual function of stabilizing the lattice and enabling a controlled shift toward oxide pathway mechanism (OPM) alongside AEM without lattice oxygen involvement. Density functional theory and spectroscopic analyses reveal that Ir preferentially substitutes Co at octahedral sites, increasing the Mn4+ population and enhancing Mn–O covalency, while facilitating *O–O formation via the OPM pathway. The optimized Ir-Co2MnO4 achieves an overpotential of 222 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and delivers high durability over 416 h at 100 mA cm–2 in 0.5 M H2SO4, including 1000 h of sustained industrial-level operation, surpassing both pristine Co2MnO4 and commercial IrO2. This work provides fundamental insights into Ir-mediated modulation of active sites and establishes a design strategy for high-performance, low-Ir OER catalysts in acidic water electrolysis.
10.1039_d5ta09283c: Cu 2 O nanocubes coated with porous covalent organic framework (COF) layers enable efficient and selective electrochemical CO 2 reduction to C 2+ products. The Cu@COF core–shell catalysts show high activity, good current density and enhanced stability.
10.1039_d6ta00929h: HA achieves triple synergy: modulating Zn 2+ solvation, restructuring H-bond network, and forming a water-poor interfacial layer. This enables >3200 h Zn‖Zn cycling and 99.27% CE in Zn‖Cu cells, highlighting a promising strategy for long-life AZIBs.
